How the ingest pipeline drains

The drain loop pulls work items in batches and hands each batch to a worker chosen round robin from the pool. A batch is only acknowledged once every item in it has been written.

Because each batch carries a checksum, a partially written batch is discarded rather than retried, which keeps the write path idempotent end to end.

Backpressure engages when the queue depth exceeds twice the configured batch size, at which point producers block until the depth falls back below the watermark.

The retry ladder is bounded: after six attempts the item is moved to a dead letter queue and an operator alert is raised.

Recommended reading: idempotency keys, dead letter queues
